glossary.confidence: An internal quality score of the AI answer: the judge's score (a second model) combined with a heuristic check of numbers and metric names against the data.
glossary.error_rate: The share of failed requests, in percent, over the test window.
glossary.hold_window: Hold window: the part of a soak test without the ramp-up and the final ramp-down, where RPS stayed at the working level. The SLA of a soak test is checked on this window.
glossary.judge: A separate model request that scores candidate answers against a rubric: grounding in data, coverage of problems, specificity, SLA awareness and usefulness of recommendations.
glossary.limiting_resource: The node resource (CPU or memory) that exceeded the SLA threshold or grew the most by the degradation step.
glossary.overshoot: The growth of p95 during the spike relative to the baseline right before it.
glossary.p95: 95th percentile: the value below which 95% of measurements fall. Shows the latency “tail” without the effect of single outliers.
glossary.peak_max: The absolute maximum of the metric over the test window. Used as a fallback when no stable step is found.
glossary.recovery_time: The time from the end of the spike until p95 returned to the baseline level (with a 10% tolerance).
glossary.resample: The aggregation interval of the time series before the analysis (for example, 5 minutes): metrics are averaged within the interval.
glossary.saturation_point: Saturation point: the last step of a stress test at which the latency and error thresholds were met.
glossary.sla_first: When SLA criteria are defined for the service, they decide the final verdict; the AI assessment is shown next to it as a supplement.
glossary.spike_window: Spike: a stretch where RPS rose 1.5 times above the baseline and stayed there for at least a minute.
glossary.stable_max: The highest load (RPS) the system held steadily for at least the set time (5 minutes by default) without degradation. Short peaks are not counted.
glossary.step_profile: Step test: the load grows in steps; the analysis looks for the last step at which the system was stable.
glossary.target_rps: The target throughput. In step and stress tests, the level to reach on a stable step; in soak, the level to hold for the whole test; in spike, the spike level.
glossary.test_type_soak: Soak test: a set load is held for a long time; the analysis checks that the load was held and looks for drift in latency, errors and resources.
glossary.test_type_spike: Spike test: the load rises sharply and returns to the baseline; the analysis assesses the growth of latency and errors during the spike and the recovery time.
glossary.test_type_step: Step test: the load grows in steps; the analysis looks for the last step at which the system was stable.
glossary.test_type_stress: Stress test: the load goes beyond the design capacity; the analysis looks for the saturation point, the nature of the degradation and the limiting resource.
glossary.trend_better: A metric change between runs is judged by its meaning: higher RPS is better, higher latency and errors are worse.
glossary.trend_drift: The change of a metric from the start to the end of the hold window under constant load. Growth of latency, errors or memory above the threshold is marked as a risk.
glossary.unverified: The numbers of this finding were not found in the collected metrics. The finding stays in the report but is not used as grounds for the verdict.
glossary.verdict_fail: The target RPS is not reached or critical SLA thresholds are violated.
glossary.verdict_na: Not enough metrics for an assessment: lt_framework data was not collected or no criteria are defined.
glossary.verdict_risk: The target RPS is reached, but secondary thresholds (latency, errors, resources) are violated, or the AI noted local degradations.
glossary.verdict_success: All defined SLA criteria are met (or, when no SLA is defined, the AI found no significant problems).
